title: Unpaid late-filing fees and delinquent campaign filers
question: Who owes the Ethics Commission late-filing fees, and does the City pay any of them?
finding: 113 entries owe late-filing fees; the rows sum to $49,225 (the file's own total line says $49,265): 30 campaign committee entries ($31,315), 65 economic-interest statement entries ($4,710; filers not named, agency column blank), 17 lobbyist entries and 1 consultant. 2 owing names are also City payees: San Francisco Travel Association owes $250, City payments $14,559,828 (2017-2027); Exploratorium owes $25, City payments $754,099 (2017-2017). A separate list names 9 campaign committees delinquent in filing, all from 2010 to 2016 elections.
how: qbyp-dnir and jb8g-e374 as published; each committee or consultant name matched exactly (letters and digits only) to vendor names in the City payment summary.
limits: The fee list has no dates and was last updated on 20 October 2021; filers drop off after four years, so it is not a current list. Most fees are $10 to $100 and some committees ended years ago. Economic-interest filers include staff and commissioners as well as elected officers. A name match does not show that the City payee and the filer are one body; the records do not show whether they are. Individuals owing fees are counted, not named.
